author: ojiudezue
title: Approved 'faster BLE arrival' build dropped: the geofence arrival already is the BLE-seen arrival
summary: The overnight probe measured 8-41 s from first home signal to URA's BLE arrival and proposed an event-driven listener. A context-wide producer/consumer inventory found HA person goes home on any non-GPS home, every resident has a Bermuda tracker, and presence.py dispatches SIGNAL_PERSON_ARRIVING source=geofence on that edge with no poll: 111/118 arrivals had geofence first within 1 s. The 8-41 s was a redundant second signal.
why: Building it would have shortened room-change visibility that perimeter face de-escalation reads, a face-naming regression, for zero latency gain. Operator required the prior-art check before build; it refuted the premise.
alternatives_considered: UniFi Wi-Fi association as an arrival signal (measured 30-243 s slower; parked)
implications: Presence docs record that the geofence arrival is the BLE-seen arrival; Wi-Fi presence parked as decision data only. Operator corrected that all BLE scanners are indoor; false arrivals come from tracker fallback blips, not scanner reach.
revisit_trigger: A resident without a BLE tracker in person.*, or measured first-arrival lag > 1 s.
